explanation:
The central tree is reduced from 119 to 83 lines (30.3%) and from 7,678 to 5,533 characters (27.9%). Six peripherals expand ownership, state publication, gesture execution, projection dependencies, routing, and application boundaries. Connections attach to the corresponding concept lines; positions leave gaps around measured text dimensions. Modular boundaries and ownership organize the overview, while peripherals expose call sequences and data dependencies.

Source-grounded corrections: MappingPage.tsx passes every non-hidden draft to the agent bridge, including inactive or unmounted documents; the seed's 'visible documents' wording was too narrow. MappingEditorRuntime.ts deletes the entire temporary clone batch when any clone is unsupported. canvasWorkspace.ts derives dirtyScenes specifically from sceneDirty, rather than overall isDirty. Session geometry is controller geometry; native anchors remain renderer-local, as canvasSession.ts establishes.

Details added beyond the seed include copyDocument's selection/control resets and conversation pending-state reset, exact session publication order, projection exclusions and default cell dimensions, focus invalidation dependencies, and routing's deferred failure invalidation. Sources are canvasWorkspace.ts and canvasSession.ts for life/state; MappingEditorCanvas.tsx and MappingEditorRuntime.ts for gestures; shapeProjection.ts and CanvasRuntimeContext.tsx for models; NativeRoutingStore.ts for routes; and MappingPage.tsx for application integration. Only context.json's supplied source text and point definition, plus seed.json, support the content. Imported controller, persistence, routing-worker and chat implementations were not supplied; their internals are not inferred. This is static source analysis, not runtime verification.
